title: Right-hand fingering and slap bass
summary: Best practice is thumb on the fingerboard and alternating two fingers; he warns against fakers and describes slap bass as a percussive style gone out of fashion.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, back specifically to the right hand, what are the different ways of playing bass that you've seen them do with the right hand? Making...
You mean the bow or the...

Well, everybody has his own style of how to hold their fingers, you know. A lot of guys just use one finger, a lot of guys use two. Of course, the best way is to put your thumb on the fingerboard, and you get a good leverage that way. And you use two fingers, the index and what you call this finger after... That's what you call it. It has had that famous finger, and you use those two, you alternate them. And that way, you can get a tremendous amount of agility and speed. And again, like I've seen some guys just use one finger... Oh, that's a mess. In other words, let's put it this way. A bass playing is an art. Practice, you know, like, it's the only way you can achieve anything is by practicing, especially an instrument. So, like, I mean, all these fakers running around. Sooner or later, they get discovered, and they're nowhere. It's best to work from the top up. And I'm glad things happened to me the way they did, because I started playing. I studied very seriously, and I was a long hair for a long time, and gradually this jazz bit came into my view, and it didn't jump on me all of a

sudden. And I'm glad it happened that way. Well, now, uh, what other way do they use other than holding their thumb against the finger bone and ticking with the first two fingers? What else have you seen
throughout the years? Oh, I really hadn't paid much attention. I'm thinking about the old slap bass.
Oh, I've seen slap bass, yeah. What is slap bass exactly? I don't know. I've never been able to do it

myself, to tell you the truth. It's just that you bounce the string up and down the fingerboard while you're playing. You hit the fingerboard with the string. Yeah, and while you're playing the notes with your left hand, you get a certain percussive effect that way. But it's gone out of style, sort of. I think a nice booming pizzicato bass is much nicer. I was to show you that jazz is going right in there, into the real nice musical all the way feeling, you know?
